title: Quantile decomposition and fanout telemetry for token SLOs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Build an instrumentation and dashboard foundation that decomposes token-level latency SLI quantiles by fanout path, region, and circuit breaker state. The goal is to make p50/p90/p95/p99 token latency attributable to the components that matter for multi-region failover and load-shedding decisions: admission controller, router fanout, shard decode, KV cache hit path, and fallback model variants. This ticket covers schema design for traces/metrics, sampling strategy to keep cardinality bounded, data pipeline changes (ingest tags), dashboard wireframes, and a runbook for using the visualization during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics schema PR merged: new labels added to token latency histogram (fanout_path, origin_region, target_region, circuit_state, model_variant)
Sampling implemented: deterministic 1% full-trace sampling plus 10% lightweight token histogram enrichment for high-throughput routes
Grafana dashboards: Quantile decomposition panel shows p50/p90/p95/p99 split across fanout_path and circuit_state, with region heatmap and slowest-shard drilldown
Runbook section updated: how to interpret circuit_state transitions and when to trigger capacity fallback or model fallbacks
Alerting: p99 token latency increase for primary region with simultaneous increase in cross-region fanout rate triggers on-call escalation rule
tasks: Design metric labels and histogram buckets for token latency
Implement emitter changes in serving runtime to attach fanout_path and circuit_state
Add deterministic sampling hook in request router for full traces

Write runbook steps and playbook for escalations and mitigations
Add e2e test harness: synthetic fanout traffic and KV miss scenarios

decision_log: Decision 2025-02-11: Use label 'fanout_path' with enumerated values {direct, fanout_peer, fanout_cross_region, fallback_variant} to avoid freeform strings
Decision 2025-02-12: Implement two-tier sampling: deterministic 1% full traces and 10% histogram enrichments for selected routes
Decision 2025-02-14: Bucket client request IDs into 100 deterministic buckets to provide stable sampling while enabling low-cardinality impact analysis
Decision 2025-02-16: Prioritize p99 and p95 decomposition panels; p50/p90 used for latency trend context only
notes: Trade-offs: keeping a small fixed vocabulary for fanout_path and circuit_state loses some fidelity (we won't capture every micro-path) but prevents explosion of metrics cardinality.
Follow-up: Consider a dedicated 'slow-path' sampler that increases sampling rate for requests that exceed p95 during incidents to aid postmortem root-cause analysis.
Related work: ties into regional failover policy effort (ENG-412992) and adaptive admit controller hysteresis (ENG-331442).
Operational guidance: On-call should first look at 'region heatmap' and 'circuit_state timeline' panels to decide whether to trigger circuit-opening or region-failover playbooks.
